# injecta

Compile-time dependency injection for Rust. You declare a container once with
`container!`, derive `Injectable` on your types, and call `resolve`. Every
dependency is checked by the compiler: a missing provider, a dependency cycle
or a singleton that depends on a request-scoped value does not compile.
There is no runtime registry, no `TypeId` map, no locks and no `dyn` on the
resolve path: a resolve compiles to constructor calls and `Arc` clones, within
about 1 ns of hand-written wiring on the comparison benchmark.

## Quick start

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use injecta::{Injectable, Resolve};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Config { url: String }

trait Logger: Send + Sync { fn log(&self, line: &str); }

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct StdoutLogger;
impl Logger for StdoutLogger { fn log(&self, _line: &str) {} }

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct Database { config: Config, logger: Arc<dyn Logger> }

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct UserRepo { db: Arc<Database> }

injecta::container! {
    pub struct App {
        instance Config,                                              // passed to App::new
        singleton Arc<dyn Logger> = |c| Arc::new(c.build::<StdoutLogger>()),
        singleton Arc<Database>,                                      // built once, on first use
        transient UserRepo,                                           // built on every resolve
    }
}

let app = App::new(Config { url: "postgres://localhost".into() });
let repo = app.resolve::<UserRepo>();
assert_eq!(repo.db.config.url, "postgres://localhost");
// singletons are shared
assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&repo.db, &app.resolve::<UserRepo>().db));
```

## The four lifetimes

| Entry | Built | `resolve` returns | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `instance T` | by you, passed to `App::new` | a clone of the value | config, values built with async or fallible code |
| `singleton T` | once, on first resolve | a clone of the cached value (`Arc<T>` to share) | pools, clients, caches |
| `scoped T` | once per scope value | a clone of the scope's cached value | per-request or per-session state |
| `transient T` | on every resolve | a new value | cheap handlers and services |

Without a factory, an entry is built with `Injectable`: `singleton Arc<X>` and
`transient Box<X>` build `X` and wrap it; any other `T` is built directly.

## Which tool to use

| You want to | Write |
| --- | --- |
| build a struct from its fields | `#[derive(Injectable)]` on the struct |
| build through a constructor (private fields, invariants) | `#[injecta::injectable]` on the `impl`, `#[inject]` on the constructor |
| give a field a fixed value | `#[inject(value = expr)]` or `#[inject(default)]` on the field |
| bind a trait object to an implementation | `singleton Arc<dyn Trait> = \|c\| Arc::new(c.build::<Impl>())` |
| register a type from another crate | a factory: `singleton Arc<Client> = \|c\| Arc::new(Client::new(c.resolve::<Config>().url))` |
| use a value that needs `async` or can fail | build it first, register it as `instance` |
| two values of the same type | newtypes: `struct PrimaryDb(Arc<Db>);` |
| per-request values | a `scope` block with `scoped` and `instance` entries |
| replace something in a test | `App::new(..).with(fake)` (singleton) or `Request::new(..).with(fake)` (scoped) |
| get a value | `container.resolve::<T>()` |
| use a shared value without cloning it (hot loops, many threads) | `container.get::<T>()` on an `instance`, `singleton` or `scoped` entry |
| one thread only (CLI, `current_thread` runtime, `no_std`) | `#[injecta(storage = injecta::SingleThread)]` on the root |
| build an unregistered `Injectable` | `container.build::<T>()` |
| accept "any container that has a `T`" | the bound `C: Provide<T>` |
| accept "any container that holds a `T` I can borrow" | the bound `C: ProvideRef<T>` |

## Borrowing cached values

`resolve` returns an owned value, so for `Arc<T>` it bumps the reference count
and the drop at the end of the statement lowers it again. `get` lends the
cached value instead: a plain load, no atomic write, nothing shared between
threads but the read. Use it at call sites that only need to look; the
container keeps the value alive.

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use injecta::{Injectable, Resolve};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Config { url: String }

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct Db { config: Config }

injecta::container! {
    struct App {
        instance Config,
        singleton Arc<Db>,
    }
}

let app = App::new(Config { url: "postgres://localhost".into() });
let db: &Arc<Db> = app.get();                 // created on first use, then borrowed
assert_eq!(db.config.url, "postgres://localhost");
assert_eq!(Arc::strong_count(db), 1);          // no clone was made
assert_eq!(app.get::<Config>().url, "postgres://localhost");
```

`get` only exists for cached entries; asking for a `transient` is a compile
error that points to `resolve`. Benchmarks: `docs/performance.md`.

## Constructors

```rust
use injecta::Resolve;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Config { pool_size: u32 }

struct Pool { size: u32 }

#[injecta::injectable]
impl Pool {
    #[inject]
    fn new(config: Config) -> Self {
        Self { size: config.pool_size.max(1) }
    }
}

injecta::container! {
    struct App { instance Config, transient Pool }
}

assert_eq!(App::new(Config { pool_size: 0 }).resolve::<Pool>().size, 1);
```

## Scopes

A `scope` is a child container. It shares the root's instances and
singletons, owns its `scoped` and `instance` entries, and rebuilds the root's
transients so they can depend on scoped values.

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use injecta::{Injectable, Resolve};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Config;
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct UserId(u64);

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct Session { user: UserId }

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct Handler { config: Config, session: Arc<Session> }

injecta::container! {
    pub struct App {
        instance Config,
    }
    pub scope Request {
        instance UserId,
        scoped Arc<Session>,
        transient Handler,
    }
}

let app = App::new(Config);
let request = Request::new(&app, UserId(7));
let a = request.resolve::<Handler>();
let b = request.resolve::<Handler>();
assert_eq!(a.session.user, UserId(7));
assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&a.session, &b.session)); // one Session per request
```

A root `singleton` that needs a `scoped` value is a compile error: the
singleton would outlive the scope (the "captive dependency" bug).

## Overrides for tests

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use injecta::Resolve;

trait Clock: Send + Sync { fn now(&self) -> u64; }
struct SystemClock;
impl Clock for SystemClock { fn now(&self) -> u64 { 1 } }
struct FixedClock(u64);
impl Clock for FixedClock { fn now(&self) -> u64 { self.0 } }

injecta::container! {
    struct App {
        singleton Arc<dyn Clock> = |_| Arc::new(SystemClock),
    }
}

let app = App::new().with(Arc::new(FixedClock(42)) as Arc<dyn Clock>);
assert_eq!(app.resolve::<Arc<dyn Clock>>().now(), 42);
```

## Compile-time errors

A missing provider names the container, the type and the fix:

```compile_fail
use injecta::Injectable;

struct Database;

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct Repo { db: std::sync::Arc<Database> }

injecta::container! {
    struct App { transient Repo }
}
// error[E0277]: `App` has no provider for `Arc<Database>`
//   = note: declare it in `injecta::container!` as `instance Arc<Database>`, ...
```

A dependency cycle fails const evaluation of the depth check:

```compile_fail
use injecta::Injectable;

#[derive(Injectable)]
struct A { b: Box<B> }
#[derive(Injectable)]
struct B { a: Box<A> }

injecta::container! {
    struct App { transient Box<A>, transient Box<B> }
}
// error[E0391]: cycle detected when ...
```

Factories (`= |c| ...`) are opaque to the cycle check: keep them small and
prefer `c.build::<T>()` inside them.

## Extension points

| Extension point | Trait | Default | Select with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cache for singleton and scoped values | [`Storage`] + [`SingletonCell`] | [`ThreadSafe`] (`OnceLock`) with `std`, [`SingleThread`] (`OnceCell`) without | `#[injecta(storage = MyStorage)]` |
| Lifecycle and diagnostics hooks | [`Hooks`] | [`NoHooks`] (compiles away) | `#[injecta(hooks = MyHooks)]` |
| Introspection | [`Container`] | generated `NAME` and `PROVIDERS` | `App::describe()` |
| Building a type | [`Injectable`] | derive or `#[injectable]` | hand-written impl |
| Resolving a type | [`Provide`] | generated per entry | hand-written impl for a custom container |

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use injecta::{Hooks, ProviderInfo, Resolve, Container};

#[derive(Default)]
struct CountCreations(AtomicUsize);
impl Hooks for CountCreations {
    fn on_create(&self, _info: &ProviderInfo) {
        self.0.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, injecta::Injectable)]
struct Cache;

injecta::container! {
    #[injecta(storage = injecta::SingleThread, hooks = CountCreations)]
    struct App { singleton Cache }
}

let app = App::new();
app.resolve::<Cache>();
app.resolve::<Cache>();
assert_eq!(app.hooks().0.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 1);
assert_eq!(App::describe().to_string(), "App\n  singleton Cache\n");
```

## Features

| Feature | Default | Adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `std` | yes | [`ThreadSafe`] storage; without it the crate is `no_std + alloc` |
| `macros` | yes | `container!`, `#[derive(Injectable)]`, `#[injectable]` |
| `tracing` | no | `TracingHooks` |

## Generic code

Write the bound, not the container type, so a function works with the root,
with any scope, and with a test container:

```rust
use injecta::{Provide, Resolve};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Config { name: &'static str }

fn greeting<C: Provide<Config>>(c: &C) -> String {
    format!("hello {}", c.resolve::<Config>().name)
}

injecta::container! {
    struct App { instance Config }
}

assert_eq!(greeting(&App::new(Config { name: "ivan" })), "hello ivan");
```

## Anti-patterns

| Don't | Do instead | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| store the container in a service and `resolve` inside methods | take each dependency as a field | hidden dependencies; the compiler can no longer check them |
| `instance Arc<Mutex<Everything>>` | one entry per service | one provider per type keeps the graph checkable |
| `unwrap()` or blocking I/O in an `#[inject]` constructor | do it before `App::new` and register the value as `instance` | constructors run lazily, at the first resolve, far from `main` |
| `singleton Pool` where `Pool` is expensive to clone | `singleton Arc<Pool>` | `resolve` returns a clone |
| a global `static APP: OnceLock<App>` | pass `&App` (or a scope) down from `main` | tests get their own container |
| registering the same type twice under different "names" | newtypes | names are not part of a Rust type |
| logic in factories | `c.build::<Impl>()` plus a constructor | factories are opaque to the cycle check |

## Limits (by design)

- One provider per type per container. Use newtypes for several values of one type.
- No async or fallible providers: do that work before building the container and register the result as `instance`.
- No runtime registration. Plugins discovered at runtime belong in a value you register (`instance Vec<Arc<dyn Plugin>>`).
- Values are returned by value (`resolve`; share with `Arc<T>`) or borrowed from the container for as long as it lives (`get`, cached entries only).

# AGENTS.md — injecta

If an `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` exists higher in the tree, follow it too; on conflict, ask the creator.

## Using injecta (for agents writing application code)

The full guide with runnable examples is `GUIDE.md` (also in `llms-full.txt`). The short version:

1. Derive `Injectable` on every struct the container should build. Fields are the dependencies.
2. If a type needs a constructor, put `#[injecta::injectable]` on its `impl` and `#[inject]` on exactly one constructor that returns `Self`.
3. Declare one `injecta::container! { pub struct App { .. } }` in the assembly crate (next to `main`), not in library crates.
4. Pick the lifetime per entry:
   - `instance T`: values you already have (config, values that needed `async` or could fail). They become `App::new` arguments.
   - `singleton Arc<T>`: one shared value, created on first resolve.
   - `transient T`: a new value per resolve.
   - `scoped Arc<T>` inside `scope Name { .. }`: one value per scope (request, session).
5. Trait objects and foreign types need a factory: `singleton Arc<dyn Trait> = |c| Arc::new(c.build::<Impl>())`.
6. Get values with `container.resolve::<T>()`. In generic code, bound on `C: Provide<T>`.
7. In tests, replace singletons with `App::new(..).with(fake)`; never add a second container type just for tests.

Hard rules:

- Never store the container inside a service; inject fields.
- Never register two entries of one type; use newtypes.
- Never `unwrap` in an `#[inject]` constructor; build fallible values first and register them as `instance`.
- When the compiler says ``App` has no provider for `X` ``, add an entry for `X` (the note lists the three forms). Do not add `Option`, `Default` or a hand-written `Provide` impl to silence it.
- A `cycle detected when simplifying constant ... DEPTH` error is a dependency cycle between the listed types. Break the cycle in the design (extract the shared part into a third type); do not hide it behind a factory.

## Changing injecta (for agents working on this repository)

- Layout: `injecta` (runtime traits, storage, hooks, introspection; `no_std + alloc` without the `std` feature) and `../injecta-macros` (`container!`, `#[derive(Injectable)]`, `#[injectable]`). `bench/` is a separate, unpublished workspace that compares injecta with other DI crates; it is never a dependency of the library.
- The hot path must stay free of locks, `dyn`, `TypeId` maps and allocation beyond what the user's own types do. Any change to generated `provide` bodies needs a run of `just bench` and the numbers in the PR.
- Every misuse that can be caught at compile time gets a `tests/ui/*.rs` case with a pinned `.stderr` that contains a fix hint. Macro errors use `syn::Error::new(span, ..)` on the offending tokens, and report all errors of one invocation at once.
- Docs have one source: `GUIDE.md`. It is the crate-level rustdoc (`include_str!`), its examples are doctests, and `tests/docs.rs` derives `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` from it and this file. After editing either, run `just docs`.
- Before calling work done: `just check` (fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` on all targets and features, nextest, doctests, compile-fail tests, MSRV check).
- Conventional Commits in English. The human is the only author: no `Co-Authored-By` or "Generated with" lines.
